Bug_Title: EC: Invocation of equals() on an array, which is equivalent to == (EC_BAD_ARRAY_COMPARE)
Bug_Details:
This method invokes the .equals(Object o) method on an array. Since arrays do not override the equals
method of Object, calling equals on an array is the same as comparing their addresses. To compare the
contents of the arrays, use java.util.Arrays.equals(Object[], Object[]).
To compare the addresses of the arrays, it would be
less confusing to explicitly check pointer equality using ==.
 java.util.Arrays.equals(Object[], Object[]) ==
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug method where the equals() method is invoked on an array. Since arrays do not override the equals method of Object, this comparison checks for reference equality rather than content equality.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUnit test cases call the showBug method with different arrays and arrays with the same reference. Since the showBug method incorrectly uses array1.equals(array2), it triggers the bug by checking reference equality instead of content equality.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm that the bug is triggered. The test methods 'testShowBugWithDifferentArrays' and 'testShowBugWithSameReferenceArrays' both pass, indicating that the'showBug' method is incorrectly comparing array references instead of their contents. This aligns with the bug rule where invoking.equals() on an array compares their memory addresses rather than their contents.
